text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it revised the outlook for Franfinance to positive from stable.
S&P also said it affirmed its A long-term and A-1 short-term ratings.

"Franfinance's ratings reflect its ownership by and increasing synergies with its parent, Societe Generale, rated AA minus/A1 plus. The ratings also reflect some improvement in its stand-alone situation," S&P said in a statement.

"If synergies with Societe Generale bear fruits and if there is a noticeable improvement in its profitability in coming years, Franfinance's long-term rating could approach those of its parent bank," S&P said.

"Franfinance's net income increased in 1995, but this was mainly due to a fall in loan loss provisions, which is not expected to be repeated in the coming years. Franfinance still has to show its ability to generate satisfactory operating profitability. Results for the first six months of 1996 are encouraging," said S&P.
S&P said it affirmed the following ratings for Franfinance. Senior unsecured A
